full_text_en:
Hainan Zili Investment Co., Ltd. v. Hainan Huaxin Property Management Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Property Management Contract

Plaintiff (Counterclaim Defendant): Hainan Zili Investment Co., Ltd.
Legal Representative: Chen Yaoxin, General Manager
Agent ad litem: Wu Weihai, lawyer of Hainan Second Law Firm

Defendant (Counterclaim Plaintiff): Hainan Huaxin Property Management Co., Ltd.
Legal Representative: Wang Jinlong, Manager
Agent ad litem: Shu Yuping, lawyer of Huahe Law Firm

Plaintiff Hainan Zili Investment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Investment Company) filed a lawsuit with the Xinhua District People's Court of Haikou City, Hainan Province, due to a dispute over a property management contract with Defendant Hainan Huaxin Property Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Property Company).

Plaintiff Investment Company alleged: In accordance with the "Shunfa New Village Property Management Contract" signed with the Defendant, the Plaintiff had contracted out to the Defendant the property management rights for the first phase of Shunfa New Village, approximately 100,000 square meters of apartments. The Defendant only paid the Plaintiff a performance bond of RMB 500,000 as stipulated in the contract, but has not paid any of the contract fees, owing a total of RMB 2,460,000 to date. The Defendant's actions constitute a serious breach of contract. The Plaintiff requests the court to dissolve the contract, order the Defendant to pay the overdue contract fees, and assume liability for breach of contract.

Defendant Property Company, while responding, also filed a counterclaim, contending: The provision in the original contract that the Defendant shall pay the Plaintiff a contract fee of RMB 1 per square meter per month violates property management regulations, is an invalid clause, and should not be protected by law. The Plaintiff failed to deliver the houses in the agreed area and on time, causing the Defendant to lose management fee income of RMB 2,034,292. According to the "Maintenance Contract" signed by both parties, the Plaintiff should have paid the second installment of maintenance fees of RMB 150,000 by the end of 1994; for each day of late payment, a penalty of 3% of the total amount shall be imposed. This amount remains unpaid to date. The counterclaim requests the court to order the Plaintiff to pay property management maintenance fees of RMB 150,000 and liquidated damages of RMB 150,000, as well as compensate the Defendant for losses of RMB 2,034,292 caused by the Plaintiff's failure to deliver the area of property management housing as stipulated in the contract.

The Xinhua District People's Court of Haikou City found through trial:

Plaintiff Investment Company is the developer of the Shunfa New Village residential community. In the first half of 1992, the Investment Company had pre-sold the houses in Shunfa New Village to nine owners, including the Hainan Branch of Changsha Nonferrous Metals Exploration and Design Institute and Hainan Xinxin Industrial Co., Ltd. In September 1993, the residential community was completed, and 320 households moved in. On January 31, 1994, the Investment Company and Defendant Property Company signed a "Shunfa New Village Property Management Contract" and a "Supplementary Agreement to the Shunfa New Village Property Management Contract." It was agreed that the Plaintiff would contract out to the Defendant the management of the first phase of 37 high-rise apartments (approximately 100,000 square meters) in Shunfa New Village for a term of ten years, with the contract fee calculated based on the actual housing area at RMB 1 per square meter per month; within ten days after signing the contract, the Property Company should pay the Investment Company a performance bond of RMB 500,000. On May 12 of the same year, the Investment Company and the Property Company signed a "Maintenance Contract," stipulating that the maintenance tasks for Buildings 1-37 of Shunfa New Village during the warranty period were to be subcontracted by the Investment Company to the Property Company, with a total subcontract price of RMB 310,000. Accordingly, the Property Company paid the Investment Company a performance bond of RMB 500,000. The Investment Company also gradually delivered to the Property Company a property management area of 61,028.25 square meters and related ancillary facilities. During the period of implementing property management, the Property Company collected property management fees, maintenance funds, water and electricity fees, etc. from the residents, but failed to pay the contract fee to the Investment Company as stipulated in the contract. The Investment Company therefore filed a lawsuit with the court.

The Xinhua District People's Court of Haikou City held after trial: The "Shunfa New Village Property Management Contract" and its supplementary agreement signed between Plaintiff Investment Company and Defendant Property Company harmed the interests of the owners of Shunfa New Village residential community and should be confirmed as invalid contracts. Property obtained by both parties under this contract should be returned to each other. The Investment Company's claim for the Property Company to pay RMB 2,460,000 in contract fees and the Property Company's counterclaim for compensation of RMB 2,034,292 for losses caused by insufficient property management housing area are both unreasonable and should be dismissed. The dispute between the Investment Company and the Property Company arising from the "Maintenance Contract" involves a different legal relationship and should not be consolidated for trial. Although the contractual relationship between the Investment Company and the Property Company is invalid, given that the Property Company has managed Shunfa New Village for many years, in order to maintain the management order of the village and facilitate the recovery of overdue property management fees, maintenance funds, water and electricity fees, etc., the Property Company may be ordered to hand over the management rights of Shunfa New Village and the maintenance fund to the Investment Company for custodial management. Accordingly, the Xinhua District People's Court of Haikou City rendered judgment on August 5, 1997:

1. The Investment Company shall return the performance bond of RMB 500,000 to the Property Company within two months from the effective date of this judgment;
2. The Property Company shall, within two months from the effective date of this judgment, deliver the collected maintenance fund and the relevant ancillary facilities of Shunfa New Village (as listed in the handover inventory) to the Investment Company for custodial management.
3. The other claims of the Investment Company and the counterclaim of the Property Company are dismissed.

After the first-instance judgment, Defendant Property Company appealed to the Haikou Intermediate People's Court of Hainan Province, arguing that the Investment Company's failure to deliver the full property management area caused losses to the Property Company for which it should bear responsibility, and that the property management rights of the residential community had already been granted to the Property Company by the Owners' Management Committee, so the Investment Company had no right to custodial management. It requested the judgment be amended.

The Haikou Intermediate People's Court found through second-instance trial: The Owners' Management Committee composed of nine owners of Shunfa New Village residential community had been approved and established by the Haikou City Real Estate Administration Bureau in July 1997, and had separately signed a "Residential Management Contract" with the Appellant Property Company.

The Haikou Intermediate People's Court held:

Property management is a new industry that emerged during the process of housing commercialization in recent years. Property management refers to a type of social service work in which a property management organization uniformly provides public services to a residential community, including the maintenance and management of social security and environmental order, and collects certain fees from residents in accordance with prescribed standards based on its management facts and service actions. The right of property management is a real right existing on property owned by others, so who can exercise that right should be determined by the property owner (i.e., the owner). Article 6 of the "Administrative Measures for New Urban Residential Communities" issued by the Ministry of Construction on March 23, 1994, stipulates: "A residential community shall establish a residential community management committee." The "Regulations on Property Management in Urban Residential Areas of the Hainan Special Economic Zone" issued by the Hainan Provincial People's Government on June 4, 1996, clearly stipulate: "Owners have the right to participate in property management of the residential area and have the obligation to use houses and public facilities reasonably, maintain public order in the residential area, and abide by the property management regulations of the residential area. The owners' meeting is the highest decision-making body for property management in the residential area, and the management committee is the executive body of the owners' meeting, with the right to select and employ a property management company, property management personnel, or other professional service organizations to carry out property management in the residential area and to sign property management contracts with them."

In this case, the Appellee Investment Company is only the development and construction unit of the Shunfa New Village residential community. It unilaterally signed a contract with the Appellant Property Company to "contract out" the property management rights of the residential community to the Property Company for exercise, taking the opportunity to collect contract fees. This act infringed upon the legitimate rights and interests of the owners. Pursuant to Article 58, Paragraph 1, Item (5) of the "General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China," this contract and its supplementary agreement should be invalid contracts. Pursuant to Article 61, Paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, the Investment Company should return the performance bond of RMB 500,000 to the Property Company, and its claims for the Property Company to pay contract fees and assume liability for breach of contract should be dismissed. The Property Company's request, based on the invalid contract, for the Investment Company to compensate for the "losses" caused by the shortfall in delivered property management area is not supported. The Investment Company has no property management rights over the residential community. Although the first-instance court noted this issue when dealing with the invalidity of the contract, it nevertheless ruled that the property management rights and maintenance fund of the residential community be handed over to the Investment Company for custodial management on grounds of maintaining the management order of the residential community and facilitating the recovery of overdue property management fees, maintenance funds, water and electricity fees, etc., which lacks legal basis and should be reversed. Now that the Owners' Management Committee of Shunfa New Village has been established and has signed a "Residential Management Contract" with the Property Company, this is an act of exercising the owners' rights. The Property Company's appeal on this ground is well-founded and should be supported. The Property Company's request for an order that the Investment Company pay it RMB 150,000 in property management maintenance fees and RMB 150,000 in liquidated damages under the contract involves a separate legal relationship; the first-instance court's decision not to consolidate the trial is correct. The first-instance judgment contains unclear findings of fact and partially improper rulings, which should be corrected.

In summary, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," the Haikou Intermediate People's Court rendered judgment on December 4, 1997:

1. Affirm Item 1 of the civil judgment (1997) Xin Min Chu Zi No. 293 of the Xinhua District People's Court of Haikou City;
2. Reverse Item 2 of the civil judgment (1997) Xin Min Chu Zi No. 293 of the Xinhua District People's Court of Haikou City;
3. Amend Item 3 to: Dismiss the claim of the Appellee Hainan Zili Investment Co., Ltd. requesting the Appellant Hainan Huaxin Property Management Co., Ltd. to pay contract fees and assume liability for breach of contract; dismiss the counterclaim of Hainan Huaxin Property Management Co., Ltd. requesting Hainan Zili Investment Co., Ltd. to compensate for economic losses caused by the shortfall in delivered property management area.
